newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma opposition politician gets 10-yr jail term.
newsitem.headline: Burma opposition politician gets 10-yr jail term.

text.p: Saw Oo Ray, a former elected representative of Burma's National League for Democracy (NLD) party, has been sentenced to 10 years in prison, official media said on Wednesday.

Saw Oo Ray, who was forced last year to resign as member of parliament (MP) for the NLD headed by democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi, was found guilty of providing money to the Karenni insurgent group in 1992 and of illegally writing a book "encouraging insurgency and narrow-minded racism" in 1993, the state-run Mirror Daily said.

An ethnic Karenni from Kayah state, Saw Oo Ray was sentenced to three years in jail under the Unlawful Associations Act and seven years under an amendment to the Printers and Publishers' Registration Act.
It did not give further details.
Suu Kyi mentioned Saw Oo Ray in a news conference on Saturday as being one of the party members arrested by the military government despite giving in to pressure to resign their parliament positions.
"I would like you to publicise the fact that the authorities are forcing our members of parliament to resign from their positions," she said.

"And even after their resignations they are still given very very heavy prison sentences," she said. "Giving into these unjust demands does not do us any good. It does not give us any lighter sentences."
The NLD won a landslide victory in a 1990 election, but was not allowed to take office because the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) never recognised the results of the poll.
After the election, the SLORC began to pressure the elected MPs, forcing many to flee the country or eventually resign from politics.
